proposals.before: Through repeated military achievements, he was promoted step by step to Biaoqi Commandant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yufu county.
proposals.after: Through repeated military achievements, he was promoted step by step to Biaoqi Commandant and enfeoffed as Count of Yufu county.
proposals.reason: Chinese 縣伯 is a county earldom/countship (伯), not a marquisate (侯); 'Marquis' mistranslates 伯.

proposals.before: When Bozhi did rebel, the Emperor ordered a commandery in the province to accept Shan.
proposals.after: When the messenger returned, Emperor Wu ordered that Shan be placed in one commandery within the province.
proposals.reason: Chinese 使反 means 'when the envoy/messenger returned', not 'when Bozhi rebelled'; context is the petition outcome before the open revolt announcement.

proposals.before: When he rebelled, Emperor Wu ordered one commandery within the province to take Shan in.
proposals.after: When the messenger returned, Emperor Wu ordered one commandery within the province to accommodate Shan.
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 使反 is the messenger's return, not Bozhi's rebellion.

proposals.before: His son Wuya was Direct Gate General. The Emperor wrote out Long Fu's crimes by hand, sealed the note, and sent it to Wuya, who opened it and showed his father.
proposals.after: Bozhi's son Wuya was then Direct Gate General. Emperor Wu personally wrote out Long Fu's crimes, sealed the note, and entrusted it to Wuya, who opened it and showed Bozhi.
proposals.reason: Chinese is 直閤/直合將軍 and 武帝手疏...親付; English 'Direct Gate' is opaque and omits that Wu Di wrote and personally delivered the sealed charge.

proposals.before: Yun disliked Chi and firmly kept him out.
proposals.after: Yun disliked Chi and firmly refused him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 堅拒之 is firm refusal of approaches, not merely keeping him out physically; minor clarity repair.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Tianjian, the Grand Marshal, the Prince of Linchuan, was ordered north. He had his secretary Qiu Chi write Bozhi a private letter:
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Tianjian, an edict ordered the Grand Marshal, the Prince of Linchuan, to invade the north. He had his secretary Qiu Chi write Bozhi a private letter:
proposals.reason: Source 詔…北侵 is an imperial order to invade; idiomatic softens to 'was ordered north' and omits the invasion sense.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Tianjian, an edict ordered the Grand Marshal the Prince of Linchuan Hunchu to invade the north; Hunchu ordered his secretary Qiu Chi privately to write him a letter, saying:
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Tianjian, an edict ordered the Grand Marshal the Prince of Linchuan Hong to invade the north; Hong ordered his secretary Qiu Chi privately to write him a letter, saying:
proposals.reason: Chinese 巨集 is a corrupted form of 宏 (Hong), personal name of the Prince of Linchuan; 'Hunchu' is not a valid reading.

proposals.before: In late spring, when Jiangnan's grass runs long and flowers speckle the trees, when parrots wheel in flocks—
proposals.after: In late spring, when Jiangnan's grass runs long and flowers speckle the trees, when orioles wheel in flocks—
proposals.reason: Classic line is 群鶯亂飛 (orioles); packet Chinese 群鸚 is likely a corruption of 鶯, and 'parrots' mistranslates the famous phrasing.

proposals.before: At the end of spring, in the third month, grasses grow long in Jiangnan; mixed flowers bloom on trees, flocks of parrots fly in disorder.
proposals.after: At the end of spring, in the third month, grasses grow long in Jiangnan; mixed flowers bloom on trees, flocks of orioles fly in disorder.
proposals.reason: Same 鸚/鶯 corruption: should be orioles (鶯), not parrots.

proposals.before: Your home still stands, your beloved wife still waits.
proposals.after: Your high hall has not fallen; your beloved concubine still lives.
proposals.reason: Chinese 愛妾 is beloved concubine, not wife; 高堂未傾 is the high hall not collapsed.

proposals.before: Wei sent the Princes of Anfeng and Huaihai, Yuan Yanming and Yuan Yu, with a hundred thousand men to oppose him.
proposals.after: Wei sent the Princes of Anfeng and Linhuai, Yuan Yanming and Yuan Yu, with a hundred thousand men to oppose him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 臨淮王 is Prince of Linhuai, not Huaihai.

proposals.before: He was transferred to the Eastern Palace's Direct Gate Guard.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Direct Gate (直閤) of the Eastern Palace.
proposals.reason: Chinese 直合 is the common corruption of 直閤; 'Direct Gate Guard' is clearer as Direct Gate office.

proposals.before: In the first year of Datong, under Commander Cao Congzong he attacked Guoyang. Wei sent the Prince of Changshan, Yuan Zhao, and others to relieve it. Their vanguard reached Tuo Stream, forty li away.
proposals.after: In the first year of Datong, under Commander Cao Zhongzong he attacked Guoyang. Wei sent the Prince of Changshan, Yuan Zhao, and others to relieve it. Their vanguard reached Tuo Stream, forty li away.
proposals.reason: Chinese 曹仲宗 is Zhongzong (仲宗); Congzong is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: The Princes of Huaihai and Anfeng, Yu and Yanming, led the officials with the imperial carriage to welcome Hao into Luoyang Palace. He took the front hall, changed the reign title, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
proposals.after: The Princes of Linhuai and Anfeng, Yu and Yanming, led the officials with the imperial carriage to welcome Hao into Luoyang Palace. He took the front hall, changed the reign title, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
proposals.reason: Chinese 臨淮王 is Prince of Linhuai, not Huaihai.

proposals.before: Once Hao had what he wanted, he sank into wine and women and neglected affairs. With the Princes of Anfeng and Huaihai he plotted to betray Liang, but while the situation remained unsettled he still relied on Qingzhi's strength.
proposals.after: Once Hao had what he wanted, he sank into wine and women and neglected affairs. With the Princes of Anfeng and Linhuai he plotted to betray Liang, but while the situation remained unsettled he still relied on Qingzhi's strength.
proposals.reason: Chinese 臨淮 is Linhuai; Huaihai is a mistranslation carried from earlier units.

proposals.before: Rong was about to withdraw when the astrologer Liu Lingzhu told him, "Within ten days Henan will be secured."
proposals.after: Rong was about to withdraw when the astrologer Liu Lingzhu (劉靈助) told him, "Within ten days Henan will be secured."
proposals.reason: Confirming the Chinese personal name 劉靈助; English Liu Lingzhu is acceptable but the source characters should remain clear.

proposals.before: At his post Qingzhi besieged Xiangcheng and defeated Wei's Inspectors of Ying and Yang, Lou Qi and Shi Yunbao, at the Zhen River.
proposals.after: At his post Qingzhi besieged Xianhu (縣瓠) and defeated Wei's Inspectors of Ying and Yang, Lou Qi and Shi Yunbao, at the Zhen River.
proposals.reason: Chinese 縣瓠 is Xianhu/Xiangcheng; confirm place rendering; Zhen River for 溱水 is acceptable.

proposals.before: His eldest son Zhaosi succeeded him.
proposals.after: His eldest son Zhao succeeded him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 長子昭嗣 is often read as eldest son Zhao (昭) succeeded (嗣), not a compound given name Zhaosi.

proposals.before: When Ziyun later returned south, Lan Qin rose through battle honors in Liang's Tianjian era to Inspector of Jizhou.
proposals.after: When Ziyun later returned south, in Liang's Tianjian era he rose through battle honors to Inspector of Jizhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 後子雲還南，梁天監中以軍功至冀州刺史 attributes the Jizhou inspectorship to father Ziyun (cf. Liang Shu), not to Lan Qin.

proposals.before: I am forgotten in this world, broken and old. My means are those of Yan Hui or Yuan Xian; my name has never reached the great ministers. If I do not drink good wine every day, where else is there for me to go?
proposals.after: I am forgotten in this world, broken and old. My means are those of Yan and Yuan (顏原); my name has never reached the great ministers. If I do not drink good wine every day, where else is there for me to go?
proposals.reason: Chinese 顏原 is the paired exemplars Yan Hui and Yuan Xian; the idiomatic expansion is acceptable but should stay clearly plural.

decisions.reason: 伯 is the count rank, not 侯 (marquis). The proposed replacement fixes the literal field to match the already accurate idiomatic field, preserving repeated battle merits, promotion, office and county fief.

decisions.after: When the messenger returned, Emperor Wu ordered that Shan be given a post in a commandery within the province.
decisions.reason: 使 is the returning messenger; 反 means return, not Bozhi's revolt. The preceding petition concerns Shan's appointment. Render 處繕 as providing an official placement, not mere lodging, while retaining the emperor's order and the commandery within the province.

decisions.after: When the messenger returned, Emperor Wu ordered that Shan be given a post in one commandery within the province.
decisions.reason: 使反 follows Bozhi's petition for Shan in s0030; it does not say Bozhi rebelled. In this appointment dispute, 一郡處繕 provides Shan an official placement in one commandery, not merely accommodation.

decisions.after: Bozhi's son Wuya was then Direct Gate General. Emperor Wu wrote out Longfu's crimes by hand and personally gave the document to Wuya, who sealed it and sent it to Bozhi.
decisions.reason: 親付 belongs to the emperor, but 武牙封示 makes Wuya the subject of sealing and forwarding the document. Both existing and proposed English invent his opening it and assign sealing to the emperor. Preserve the son, office, handwritten accusations and personal delivery; retain Nanshi's Wuya, not Liangshu's variant Huya.

decisions.reason: In the context of repeated calls on Fan Yun (s0277), 'firmly kept him out' adequately conveys 堅拒之. 'Firmly refused him' is only a stylistic alternative. The separate misreading Chi for 緭 remains in both versions and is explicitly logged for chapter-wide correction.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 雲不好緭，堅拒之。

decisions.after: In the fourth year of Tianjian, the Grand Marshal Hong, Prince of Linchuan, was ordered to invade the north. He had his secretary Qiu Chi write Bozhi a private letter:
decisions.reason: 北侵 specifies an invasion, not merely movement north. Also restore Hong, omitted from this field: the parallel Liangshu passage names 宏 where the current transcription has 巨集. Preserve the year, imperial order, titles, secretary and private letter to Bozhi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 天監四年，詔太尉、臨川王宏率衆軍北討，宏命記室丘遲私與伯之書曰：

decisions.reason: The parallel Liangshu narrative explicitly names the Prince of Linchuan 宏, Hong; his biography in Liangshu 22 independently confirms that name. Replacing both instances of Hunchu restores the person behind the transcription's 巨集 without importing other facts or changing the Chinese source.

decisions.after: In the third month, late in spring, Jiangnan's grass runs long, flowers of many kinds bloom on the trees, and flocks of orioles fly about.
decisions.reason: The independent letter text reads 群鶯, and Liangshu 20 has 羣鸎, supporting orioles instead of the current Nanshi transcription's parrots. Restore 三月 as the third lunar month as well; do not silently convert it to Gregorian March. No source edit or date approval is implied.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 暮春三月，江南草長，雜花生樹，群鶯亂飛。

decisions.reason: The independently consulted letter has 群鶯 and Liangshu 20 has 羣鸎, both oriole readings against current 群鸚. The proposed literal correction preserves the third month, late spring, Jiangnan, grass, flowers, trees and disordered flight.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 暮春三月，江南草長，雜花生樹，群鶯亂飛。

decisions.after: Your home still stands, and your beloved concubine still lives.
decisions.reason: 愛妾 means beloved concubine, not wife; 尚在 states continued presence or survival, not that she is waiting. 'Your home still stands' already conveys the surviving residence in this reassurance and need not become a wooden 'high hall has not fallen'. The literal field already preserves concubine and survival.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 高堂未傾，愛妾尚在。

decisions.reason: 臨淮王 is Prince of Linhuai, not Huaihai. The two princes, Yuan Yanming and Yuan Yu, their order and the hundred-thousand-strong force remain intact. The same correction is needed in the unproposed literal field.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 魏遣安豐王元延明、臨淮王元彧率眾十萬來拒。

decisions.reason: The existing office rendering is adequate for 轉東宮直合. Deleting 'Guard' does not establish a substantive fidelity correction, and inserting untranslated office characters is not philology in this narrative. Liangshu 32's 直閤 supports the orthographic identification, not the need for this English change.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 轉東宮直合。

decisions.reason: 仲宗 is Zhongzong, not Congzong. The repair preserves the first year of Datong, command relationship, attack on Guoyang, Wei relief under Yuan Zhao and the vanguard's location forty li away. Later 仲宗 callbacks and the paired literal field still require the same name correction.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 大通元年，隸領軍曹仲宗伐渦陽，魏遣常山王元昭等來援，前軍至駝澗，去渦陽四十里。

decisions.reason: 臨淮王彧 is Yu, Prince of Linhuai, matching s0101, not Huaihai. The other prince, officials, imperial carriage, reception into Luoyang Palace, front hall, era change and amnesty remain present.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其臨淮王彧、安豐王延明率百僚備法駕迎顥入洛陽宮，御前殿，改元大赦。

decisions.reason: 臨淮 is the same Linhuai title as s0101 and s0140. This corrects the title without altering Hao's dissipation, neglect of affairs, conspiracy against Liang, unsettled conditions or continuing reliance on Qingzhi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 顥既得志，荒於酒色，不復視事，與安豐、臨淮計將背梁，以時事未安，且資慶之力用。

decisions.reason: Liu Lingzhu already accurately represents 劉靈助. The prediction and addressee are preserved in the original. Appending Chinese characters supplies no missing historical fact and is not an actual philological discussion.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 榮將退還，時有善天文人劉靈助謂榮曰：「不出十日，河南大定。」

decisions.after: At his post Qingzhi besieged Xuanhu and defeated Wei's Inspectors of Ying and Yang, Lou Qi and Shi Yunbao, at the Zhen River.
decisions.reason: 縣瓠 denotes Xuanhu, written 懸瓠 in the parallel Liangshu narrative; it is not Xiangcheng, and the proposal's Xianhu uses the wrong reading here. Remove its unnecessary Chinese insertion. Preserve Qingzhi, both defeated inspectors and the Zhen River.

decisions.after: Ziyun later returned south and, through battle honors in Liang's Tianjian era, rose to Inspector of Jizhou.
decisions.reason: 子雲 remains the subject through 以軍功至冀州刺史; the following unit explicitly restarts 欽. Liangshu 32 confirms that Qin's father Ziyun held this office. Make the father's return and subsequent promotion a coherent sequence without implying that Lan Qin received the appointment.

decisions.reason: 顏原 alludes to Yan Hui and Yuan Xian as exemplars of poverty. The existing distributive 'Yan Hui or Yuan Xian' compares the writer's means to either man and does not merge them. Shortening their names and adding Chinese is not a fidelity repair; retain both existing English fields.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 吾既寂漠當世，朽病殘年，產不異于顏原，名未動於卿相，若不日飲醇酒，復欲安歸？

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其臨淮王彧、安豐王延明率百僚備法駕迎顥入洛陽宮，御前殿，改元大赦。
